title: On-call-friendly scheduled delivery digests and compact CSV manifests
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Our existing scheduled CSV exports create large monolithic blobs and send raw multipart webhooks which are hard for on-call and downstream consumers to triage. Failures are noisy for SREs because a single tenant-level failure can surface as multiple webhook errors and require manual rehydration. We also have costly repeated retransmits when partial uploads fail.

Goal: Produce compact, on-call-friendly delivery digests plus a lightweight per-export manifest that makes retry/resume simple for both SREs and customer integrations. Keep existing CSV consumer compatibility while reducing operational noise and improving measurable end-to-end SLOs for scheduled exports.

Proposed approach:
- Generate two artifacts per scheduled export window: 1) a compact CSV(s) with column-level optional compression and canonical ordering; 2) a small manifest CSV (<= 1KB typical) listing object keys, byte-ranges (for chunk-resumability), MD5/SHA256 checksums, row-count, and a human-friendly summary line for on-call.
- Object naming: <tenant_id>/exports/YYYY-MM-DD/TIME/digest-<seq>.csv and manifest as manifest-<window>.csv. Include content-version header in metadata to support later schema evolution.
- Delivery flow: first upload compact CSV parts to S3 using multipart with SSE-KMS. After finalizing uploads, upload manifest and then send a single webhook with manifest URL + lightweight summary. Webhook is idempotent and includes a manifest checksum for validation.
- Incremental/delta mode: support 'delta' exports that include only changed tenant rows using a compact state token. Delta exports reference prior manifest checksums to enable fast reconciliation by consumers.
- Backpressure and retries: implement exponential backoff with jitter, per-tenant rate limits and a bounded queue. On webhook delivery failure, we will retry with increasing intervals and surface grouped errors to a single on-call alert per tenant per window (instead of N alerts per object).
- Observability and SLOs: emit metrics for export_latency_ms, bytes_uploaded, manifest_generation_latency_ms, webhook_delivery_latency_ms, webhook_failure_count, and manifest_validation_failures. Add dashboard and alert: high manifest_validation_failures > 1% over 1h triggers P1 on-call.
- Compatibility: keep legacy full-blob exports available via feature flag for customers requiring unchanged behavior. Provide a migration helper that lets customers opt-in per-tenant.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Scheduled run produces a compact CSV and a manifest for 95% of tenant windows; manifest size < 2KB for typical windows.
2) Single webhook per window with manifest URL is delivered; retries are idempotent and visible in delivery metrics.
3) On-call noise reduced: grouped alerts per tenant per window for delivery failures instead of per-object alerts.
4) Download/resume: consumers can resume partial downloads using manifest byte-range info and validate checksums.
5) Backwards compatible for existing customers until migration flag flipped.

Implementation notes:
- New service module export-digest-generator that runs in the export workers pool. Uses existing s3-uploader library but adds atomic manifest upload step.
- Small DB table export_manifests(tenant_id, window_id, manifest_key, checksum, state, created_at) to track lifecycle and retries. Keep as minimal as possible to avoid long migrations.
- Runbook: provide a console step-by-step to rehydrate failed windows and to mark manifests as redelivered.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: internal beta for a subset of low-volume tenants behind feature flag (2 weeks).
- Phase 2: ramp to 25% of tenants and run comparison metrics against legacy pipeline (3 weeks).
- Phase 3: full migration and flag removal for eligible customers (2 weeks), keep legacy available for enterprise exceptions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: KMS encryption errors prevent uploads. Mitigation: fallback to customer-specific retry queues and surface clear SRE dashboards.
- Risk: Consumers depend on ordering quirks. Mitigation: export a compatibility mapping and offer migration window to opt-in.

Estimated effort: 5 points across export workers, uploader, small DB migration, and monitoring/dashboards.
